title: Scheduling the Kingsway bridge inspection
text:
Our maintenance policy is explicit: any road bridge carrying more than 10,000 vehicles per day must undergo a full structural inspection every four years. This threshold was set by the transport authority in 2019 and has not been revised since.

Traffic counts for the Kingsway bridge were collected continuously throughout last year using inductive loop sensors at both approaches. The annual mean was 14,200 vehicles per day, and the lowest monthly mean, recorded in February, was 11,800. The bridge therefore exceeds the threshold in every month of the year, not merely on average.

The most recent full structural inspection of the Kingsway bridge was completed in March 2022, which is more than four years ago.

It follows that the Kingsway bridge is now due for a full structural inspection. This conclusion depends only on the policy as written and the traffic figures above; it does not depend on any judgement about the bridge's current condition, which may well be excellent. If the authority wishes to avoid the inspection, it must change the policy or dispute the traffic counts, not appeal to the bridge's appearance.

One caveat should be stated plainly. The sensors were offline for eleven days in August following a power fault. If traffic during that period had been unusually low, the annual mean would fall slightly, but not far enough to approach the threshold, since the February minimum already clears it.

result.summary: The reasoning contains two hasty generalizations that weaken the claim that the bridge is due for inspection.

flaws.quote: The bridge therefore exceeds the threshold in every month of the year, not merely on average.
flaws.explanation: The author concludes that the bridge exceeds the threshold each day (or each month) based solely on monthly average traffic figures; this assumes that monthly averages imply daily exceedance without justification, which is a hasty generalization.

flaws.quote: If traffic during that period had been unusually low, the annual mean would fall slightly, but not far enough to approach the threshold, since the February minimum already clears it.
flaws.explanation: The author assumes that even unusually low traffic during the sensor downtime would not lower the annual mean enough to near the threshold, merely because the February monthly mean is above threshold; this ignores how a low August could affect the yearly average and is a hasty generalization.

strengths: The argument explicitly separates the inspection requirement from subjective judgments about the bridge's current condition, focusing solely on policy and traffic data.
